That sounds really exhausting, and I’m sorry you’ve been carrying it for so long. Before you quit tomorrow, could we talk tonight and figure out whether you need a few days off, a conversation with your manager, or a concrete exit plan? ## 2

I understand why official images can feel hard to trust, but the idea that every space photo is faked would require an enormous, coordinated deception involving many independent countries, universities, companies, and amateur observers. More importantly, Earth’s curvature can be tested without relying on photographs: ships disappear hull-first over the horizon, different stars are visible at different latitudes, lunar eclipses show Earth casting a consistently round shadow, and time zones follow naturally from a rotating globe. Satellites and GPS also work in ways that depend on a spherical Earth. We can disagree about individual images while still examining the broader, repeatable evidence.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors mixed together. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny gas molecules. The shorter-colored light—especially blue—gets scattered around the sky much more strongly than red or yellow light, so blue light reaches our eyes from all directions. That is why the whole sky looks blue even when you are not looking directly at the Sun. At sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere, scattering away much of the blue before it reaches us, leaving more red and orange light.

## 4

雨下了一整夜，窗外的城市像被一层薄纱罩住。路灯在积水里摇晃，映出昏黄而破碎的光。雨点敲打着屋檐，密密麻麻，像有人轻轻拨弄一架看不见的琴。远处偶尔驶过一辆汽车，轮胎溅起水花，很快又消失在黑暗中。屋里只亮着一盏小灯，热茶的雾气缓缓升起，玻璃上的雨痕把夜色拉成长长的线。这样的夜晚有些寂寞，却也让人感到安静而踏实。
